name: Jumbo Rocks Campground
highlights: Sites tucked between giant granite boulders. Skull Rock trail starts right from camp, and the stargazing is excellent.
tip: Nights drop below freezing in December and January, so bring a warm bag. No water at the campground.

name: Indian Cove Campground
highlights: Hidden in the Wonderland of Rocks. Popular base camp for climbers, with its own entrance off Highway 62.
tip: No through-road into the main park from here. Stock up in Twentynine Palms or Joshua Tree town.

name: Borrego Palm Canyon Campground
highlights: Walk to a palm oasis on the Palm Canyon trail and watch for bighorn sheep. Late-winter wildflowers in wet years.
tip: Check the park's wildflower updates in February. Borrego Springs is an International Dark Sky Community.

name: Hole-in-the-Wall Campground
highlights: Volcanic cliffs and the Rings Loop Trail, where you climb out of a slot canyon on metal rings. Very quiet compared with Joshua Tree.
tip: Remote, with no gas or food nearby. Fill up in Barstow or Needles. Sits around 4,400 ft, so expect cold nights.

name: Furnace Creek Campground
highlights: Sunrise at Zabriskie Point, Badwater Basin salt flats, and Mesquite Flat dunes. Winter is the only comfortable season.
tip: Summer is dangerously hot. Plan on winter only. Reserve early for holidays and Presidents' Day weekend.

name: Leo Carrillo State Park
highlights: Canyon campsites a short walk from tidepools, sea caves, and a classic surf point.
tip: Winter brings the lowest daytime tides, which are best for tidepooling. Check a tide chart before you go.

name: Selby Campground
highlights: In wet years, the hills turn yellow and purple during superblooms. Soda Lake and Painted Rock are nearby.
tip: Primitive camping with no water and very rough dirt roads after rain. Bring everything you need and check road conditions.

name: Ricardo Campground
highlights: Striped red cliffs that have appeared in countless Westerns. Spring wildflowers and big desert sunsets.
tip: Wind can be fierce, so stake your tent well. Close to the Eastern Sierra if you want to keep driving up 14/395.

name: Scorpion Ranch Campground
park: Channel Islands National Park (Santa Cruz Island)
highlights: Ferry from Ventura, then kayak sea caves and hike to Potato Harbor. Island foxes walk right through camp.
tip: Book the boat (Island Packers) and campsite separately. Use the fox-proof food boxes, because ravens and foxes steal everything.

name: Sycamore Canyon Campground
highlights: Beach on one side, Santa Monica Mountains trails on the other. Spring green-up and wildflowers on the Ray Miller Trail.
tip: A good first camping trip with kids: real bathrooms, the beach, and it's close to home.

name: Serrano Campground
highlights: Pine forest right on the lake's north shore, with paddleboarding, the Alpine Pedal Path, and cool nights at 6,750 ft.
tip: One of the few local campgrounds with hot showers. Summer weekends book out months ahead.

name: Idyllwild Campground
highlights: Walk into the artsy mountain town of Idyllwild. Hike Ernie Maxwell Trail or go for Tahquitz Peak.
tip: Fire restrictions are common in summer, so check before planning a campfire. San Jacinto peak trails need wilderness permits.

name: Lodgepole Campground
highlights: A short drive to the General Sherman Tree and Moro Rock. Tokopah Falls trail starts right in camp.
tip: This is serious bear country. Use the bear boxes for everything with a scent, including sunscreen.

name: Convict Lake Campground
highlights: A turquoise alpine lake under dramatic peaks. Easy 2.5-mile loop around the lake, with Mammoth Lakes nearby.
tip: Make the drive up 395 a trip of its own. Stop at Alabama Hills and grab a bite in Lone Pine or Bishop.

name: Jalama Beach County Park
highlights: A remote beach at the end of a winding 14-mile road. Wild surf, whale spotting, and the famous Jalama Burger at the grill.
tip: It's windy and the June fog is real, so bring layers. September and October are usually the sunniest months.

name: Sabrina & North Lake Campgrounds
highlights: Some of the best fall color in California. Aspens turn gold from late September to mid-October.
tip: Above 9,000 ft, so nights get very cold in fall. Altitude headaches are common, so drink lots of water.

name: William Heise County Park
highlights: Oak and pine forest a few miles from Julian, famous for apple pie, cider, and the fall apple harvest.
tip: Apple season brings crowds on weekends, so go midweek if you can. There are cabins if you don't want to tent.

name: Paso Picacho Campground
highlights: Hike straight from camp to the summit of Stonewall Peak for a 360° view. Black oaks change color in fall.
tip: Pair it with a Julian apple run, just 15 minutes away.

name: El Capitán State Beach
highlights: Bluff-top sites above a sandy cove, with sycamores, tidepools, and a bike path to Refugio.
tip: LA's warmest, clearest beach weather is often in September and October, after the kids go back to school.
